question: Which explanation of calcium signaling in skeletal-muscle contraction is scientifically accurate?
options: Skeletal muscles contract when calcium is removed from the cell.
Nerves contract muscles by pulling the fibers directly.
Calcium release lets muscle filaments slide and contract.
Calcium causes muscles to relax by detaching all filaments permanently.
gold_answer: Calcium release lets muscle filaments slide and contract.
notes: Team-authored original item on calcium signaling in skeletal-muscle contraction. Passages are team-authored derivations recorded under sciclaim-appx-A. Requires independent annotation and adjudication before any gate result is reported.

positions.answer: Calcium release lets muscle filaments slide and contract.

claims.text: A nerve signal triggers calcium release inside the muscle fiber.

evidence.text: The action potential opens calcium channels of the sarcoplasmic reticulum, flooding the fiber interior with calcium.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes signal-triggered calcium release, which entails the claim.

claims.text: ATP is unnecessary for muscle contraction.

evidence.text: ATP powers the myosin pivot and detaches myosin from actin; without it, contraction cannot proceed.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage makes ATP essential, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: One protein controls every aspect of contraction.

evidence.text: Expression levels of several contractile proteins were measured in the biopsies.

claims.verdict_rationale: Measuring several proteins cannot show one controls everything, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Skeletal muscles contract when calcium is removed from the cell.

claims.text: Calcium exposes the binding sites on actin filaments.

evidence.text: Calcium binds troponin, shifting tropomyosin away from the myosin-binding sites on actin.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes calcium uncovering the binding sites, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Smooth and skeletal muscle use identical calcium triggers.

evidence.text: Skeletal muscle uses troponin-based control, while smooth muscle uses a different myosin-linked regulatory system.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes different control systems, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Calcium supplements improve sprint speed in all athletes.

evidence.text: Supplement use and sprint times were both recorded in the survey.

claims.verdict_rationale: Recording both variables cannot show improvement in all athletes, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.

positions.answer: Nerves contract muscles by pulling the fibers directly.

claims.text: Myosin heads pull actin filaments to shorten the sarcomere.

evidence.text: Energized myosin heads attach to exposed actin sites and pivot, sliding the filaments past each other.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage describes myosin pivoting sliding the filaments, which entails the claim.

claims.text: Muscles contract when calcium is pumped back into storage.

evidence.text: Pumping calcium back into the reticulum ends contraction and causes relaxation, not contraction.

claims.verdict_rationale: The passage assigns pumping to relaxation, which refutes the claim.

claims.text: Muscle cramps are always caused by dehydration.

evidence.text: Cramp episodes were logged alongside hydration status in the cohort.

claims.verdict_rationale: Logging both cannot show dehydration always causes cramps, so the claim is neither established nor refuted.
